content:
liz: Heads-up everyone — we're starting a phased migration of our CI from GitHub Actions -> Buildkite next week (planned kickoff Mon 2024-11-25). This affects all repos under redwood-org that currently run GH Actions for CI. The goal: faster parallel builds, more reliable pipelines, and ~25% lower CI cost across typical workloads. Docs & schedule: https://internal.redwood.ai/ci-migration-guide :spiral_calendar:

raj: How many repos are in scope? any opt-out window? :thinking:

liz: Good Q. In-scope: ~220 repos. We have an opt-in period this week for early migrations, then a soft migration (non-blocking) phase for the next 3 weeks, and a forced migration on 2024-12-20. If you need an exemption (eg: legal/compliance reasons), please tag @ops-team and include the repo name.

maria: Will this change PR check UX? i.e. status checks and required contexts?

liz: We will keep the same required contexts (we're preserving the GH status API integration). Buildkite pipelines will emit statuses back to GitHub, so PRs still show checks. We'll swap the badge URLs though — see README guidance in the doc.

alex: Do org-level PATs or service accounts need rotation? Our workflows use a GH PAT stored in repo secrets for releases.

sre-oncall: Yes — any PATs that are injected into Actions workflows should be rotated. As part of migration we'll create dedicated Buildkite agent tokens and a set of service accounts. Action for repo owners: replace GH workflow secrets named GHA_TOKEN / RELEASE_TOKEN with BK_AGENT_TOKEN by the soft migration date. Runbook: https://internal.redwood.ai/ci-runbooks/token-rotation

liz: Quick example of updating a secret via gh cli:```bash
# create new secret in GitHub (if you still use GH Secrets for creds to call release API)
gh secret set BK_AGENT_TOKEN -b"$(cat /tmp/bk_token)" -R redwood-org/your-repo
```

raj: Any changes to how matrix/parallel builds are configured? we use a lot of matrix jobs for model tests.

liz: Buildkite uses a different config (pipeline.yml) but supports matrix via dynamic steps and parallelism. We'll provide a converter script that translates common GH Actions matrix patterns to pipeline.yml examples. See converter: https://internal.redwood.ai/ci-migration-guide#converter :gear:

buildkite-bot: Pipeline "redwood-org/rlhf-evals" created by migration-script · view: https://buildkite.com/redwood-org/rlhf-evals :white_check_mark:

maria: Will on-call alerts change? i saw a note about notifications to ops.

sre-oncall: Alerts will bridge to PagerDuty same as before; our runbook ensures Buildkite failures trigger the same alerting rules. If you have custom alerting tied to GH Actions webhooks, please open a ticket so we can help replicate it.

liz: Migration checklist (short):
- [ ] Review repo-specific notes in the doc and tag @ops-team if you need an exemption
- [ ] Replace GHA_TOKEN/RELEASE_TOKEN secrets by 2024-12-15 or earlier
- [ ] Update README CI badge (examples in doc)
- [ ] Validate the first Buildkite run in the opt-in window and report issues in this thread

ops-team: We're scheduling migration slots — please sign up here: https://cal.com/redwood-ci-migration (pick a 2h slot). We'll do the heavy lifting for you during your slot. :calendar:

alex: If something breaks post-migration, what's rollback?

liz: We'll keep GH Actions pipelines archived for 7 days after migration so we can revert in an emergency. Also, each migration will be a canary on a single repo first, then group rollouts. Use the incident runbook linked in the migration doc.

maria: Thanks — tagging eng teams to review their repos. :eyes: :thumbsup:

liz: Thanks all. If you're a repo owner and haven't seen a direct ping from @ops-team by EOD Friday, DM me and we'll prioritize you. Final note: expect brief CI token rotation windows and a few flaky runs while we stabilize. We'll post regular updates to #eng-platform and #eng-sre.
